Sam / Marissa — thanks again for the session this morning. Two quick technical notes I wanted to capture in thread for your security team: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC Peering:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is generally preferable for cross-account connectivity when you want to avoid route-table exposure and maintain tighter security boundaries. It also avoids propagating routes across accounts.
- VPC peering can be simpler for broad internal traffic but requires ensuring no overlapping CIDRs and careful route table management. Given FinPay's non-overlapping CIDRs, peering is feasible, but PrivateLink still gives more granular access control.

2) Required networking artifacts we'll request:
- VPC endpoint security group rules (we'll provide example rules; typically allow outbound HTTPS 443 from your app subnet to the endpoint security group)
- The service consumer will create an interface endpoint in each VPC; the endpoint needs ENIs and will use your subnet IPs.
- We will publish an endpoint service from Redwood's account. To accept connections we will request the Service Consumer to allow the Redwood service principal (we'll provide the ARN) or accept the VPC endpoint connection when we create it.

3) IAM permissions (high level):
- ec2:CreateVpcEndpoint, ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints, ec2:ModifyVpcEndpoint
- iam:PassRole (if you want us to assume a cross-account role for limited setup; we can avoid this if your infra team prefers to create the endpoint manually)

Next steps from us: I will upload an example IAM policy and the minimal security group template to the shared Drive and ping once ready. If you prefer, we can do a short follow-up with your security team to walk through the IAM policy.
